slides.title: The Classical Perception Pipeline    Example On One Lidar Scan

visualInspection.notes: Five-stage pipeline: acquisition, filtering, segmentation, feature extraction, interpretation. The example starts with 360 ranges, discards four zero-valued bad returns, and retains 356. A gap greater than 20 cm splits three clusters. Line fits produce three wall segments; two long parallel walls and one short wall are interpreted as a corridor. That interpretation is illustrative, not a uniqueness proof. slides.title: Probabilistic Paradigm

visualInspection.notes: Belief is a conditional probability distribution over planar pose (x, y, θ), recursively informed by control and noisy observations. slides.title: Bayes Filter Algorithm

visualInspection.notes: Bayes prediction integrates the motion model against the previous belief; correction multiplies by likelihood and normalizes. The no-assumption claim cannot mean absence of motion, measurement, or Markov assumptions. It is qualified as freedom from a fixed linear/Gaussian family. Zero total evidence cannot be normalized directly. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Belief Distributions - Gaussian Filter

visualInspection.notes: Multivariate Gaussian density has an inverse and determinant normalization. Mean and symmetric covariance are shown, including all pose variances and cross-covariances. Covariance is a central second moment and is positive semidefinite; the ordinary full-dimensional density requires positive definiteness. Singular cases need separate support treatment. A single Gaussian is unimodal; a mixture is a different representation. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Belief Distributions - Particle Filter

visualInspection.notes: Particles are candidate states approximating a possibly multimodal, non-Gaussian belief. The graph places sample marks beneath a skewed curve. A blanket threshold of 100 or more particles is not a universal accuracy certificate. Finite-sample error, bias, complexity, and sampling quality are distinct; more particles cost more computation without guaranteeing lower error on every realization. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Bayes-Filter Implementation: Kalman Filter

visualInspection.notes: Linear transition x_t = F_t x_(t−1) + G_t u_t + v_t and measurement z_t = H_t x_t + w_t use zero-mean Gaussian noises with covariances V_t and W_t. The initial belief is Gaussian. The LTI introductory wording is narrower than known time-varying linear filtering. Exact Gaussian posterior and optimality statements require the usual noise-independence and correct-model assumptions. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)

visualInspection.notes: First-order EKF Taylor expansions were inspected. Motion Jacobians use the previous corrected state and zero noise; measurement Jacobians use the predicted state and zero noise. The printed motion evaluation x_t = μ_(t−1) has a time-index mismatch with differentiation with respect to x_(t−1). Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Measurement Model – Landmark based                                                              Landmark

visualInspection.notes: Known global landmark coordinates and unknown robot pose define localization. Range is Euclidean distance and bearing is relative to robot heading, with additive range/bearing noise. The printed single-argument arctangent loses quadrant information and fails when its denominator is zero; the explicit correction is atan2 with wrapping. Coincident robot and landmark positions make bearing and the regular Jacobian undefined. Landmark extraction is the example’s representation choice, not mandatory for every localization system. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside extracted text.
